newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea says S.Korea behind Japan abduction case.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea says S.Korea behind Japan abduction case.

text.p: North Korea on Monday denied involvement in the suspected kidnapping of Japanese girl in 1977, saying South Korean authorities fabricated the case to impair ties between Tokyo and Pyongyang.

The alleged abduction of Japanese schoolgirl Megumni Yokota in 1977 by North Korean officials, which Tokyo has cited as a key reason for not joining recent efforts to aid impoverished Pyongyang, is "based on preposterous speculation", official media said.

"It is obvious that the South Korean puppets abruptly concocted the false case in a bid to prevent Japan from setting out on the improvement of relations with North Korea," the state-run Korean Central News Agency quoted a North Korean Foreign Ministry spokesman as saying.
A separate KCNA report, monitored in Tokyo, accused Seoul of fabricating the kidnapping to dampen the international community's response to calls for food aid to the North.
Japan has seized on the suspected kidnapping, first made public by South Korean authorities, to avoid criticism of its 1910-45 colonisation of Korea, the KCNA report said.
Repeated international appeals for food aid to stave off famine in North Korea -- the latest a U.N. World Food Programme appeal for $95.5 million -- have drawn only a lukewarm response.

Japan said last week that Tokyo may not give food aid to North Korea, citing the suspicion a number of Japanese were abducted by North Korea in the 1960s and 1970s and a big drug seizure aboard a North Korean freighter this month.
